safePurpose: Organise self-entered exposure timing, affected-area context and symptoms into a conservative emergency, public-health-contact or same-day-clinical pathway.
privacy: Treat every selection as sensitive health and contact-tracing context. Keep it local; do not request names, contact details, exact locations or identifiers and do not store, log, upload, sync, email, add it to URLs or send it to analytics.
disallowed: setting monitoring, isolation or movement duration
giving testing, transport or treatment instructions instead of public-health authorities
using a self-entered more-than-21-days selection as clearance
delaying contact tracing, testing, isolation guidance, public-health contact or emergency care
staticText: Ebola Exposure and Public-Health Checklist for /tools/ebola-checklist/. Explain only a conservative local escalation worksheet: emergency signs lead to emergency services; possible exposure within or with unknown relation to the 2–21 day incubation range plus symptoms, affected-area context plus symptoms, or an official contact designation leads to immediate official public-health contact; symptoms without known context lead to same-day clinical assessment. The 2–21 day range is context, never self-clearance. Do not diagnose or rule out Ebola, claim live outbreak status, decide whether exposure occurred, set monitoring or isolation duration, prescribe treatment, or delay contact tracing, testing, isolation guidance, public-health contact or emergency care. Exposure and symptoms are sensitive and local: do not request names, contact details, exact location or identifiers, and do not store, log, upload, sync, email, add selections to URLs or send them to analytics. Sources reviewed 2026-07-26: WHO Ebola disease fact sheet and questions and answers.
